frozen_candidate_root_contribution: The root contributes ELEVATED INTRINSIC WORTH: the marking of an entity as being of high, esteem-commanding value/nobility/excellence. In stative-adjectival forms it names the quality (a bearer that is precious, noble, honorable, choice); in causative-verbal and derived-nominal forms it names the conferring or recognition of that elevated-worth status upon a participant (to raise into / treat as possessing high worth = to honor/ennoble).

internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: The root contributes ELEVATED INTRINSIC WORTH: the marking of an entity as being of high, esteem-commanding value/nobility/excellence. In stative-adjectival forms it names the quality (a bearer that is precious, noble, honorable, choice); in causative-verbal and derived-nominal forms it names the conferring or recognition of that elevated-worth status upon a participant (to raise into / treat as possessing high worth = to honor/ennoble).
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Every occurrence, once form/construction/participant/context are subtracted, leaves the same residue: "of high, esteem-worthy value." (1) The dominant adjective kareem/kiraam attributes this worth across radically different participants — an angel (12:31 malak kareem), speech (17:23 qawlan kareeman), provision and reward (22:50; 33:31 rizq/ajr kareem), a throne (23:116 al-ʿarsh al-kareem), a station (26:58 maqaam kareem), a choice/noble kind of plant (26:7; 31:10 zawj kareem), a letter (27:29 kitaab kareem), scripture (56:77 qurʾaan kareem), a messenger (44:17; 69:40; 81:19 rasool kareem), and God Himself (44:49 al-kareem; 82:6; 96:3 al-akram). In each the item is not merely present but marked as high-value/noble/excellent. (2) The elative akram (49:13 akramakum ʿind Allah = the most elevated-in-worth before God = the most pious; 96:3 al-akram = the supremely worthy) is the same quality at superlative degree. (3) The plural substantive kiraam works identically: noble recording angels (82:11 kiraaman kaatibin; 80:16 kiraam barara) and people of dignified comportment (25:72 marru kiraaman = passed by with nobility). (4) The causative verbs karrama (17:70 karramnaa banii aadama = ennobled/gave-worth to the sons of Adam; 17:62 Iblis: "this one whom You karramta ʿalayya" = elevated in worth above me) and akrama (12:21 akrimii mathwaahu = give-worth to his lodging = treat him honorably; 89:15 rabbii akramani = my Lord raised me in worth; 89:17 laa tukrimoona al-yateem = you do not accord worth to the orphan) all denote conferring the krm-quality on someone. (5) The passive/derived nouns mukramoon / mukrameen / mukarrama / ikraam are the received or bestowed form of that same status: honored servants (21:26; 37:42; 70:35), the honored (36:27), Abraham's honored guests (51:24), honored scrolls (80:13 mukarrama), and God as dhu'l-jalaali wa'l-ikraam (55:27; 55:78 = Possessor of Majesty and the according-of-worth). The single invariant is therefore "elevated, esteem-worthy value," with the verb/nominal families adding only the causative/recognitional direction supplied by their morphology.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: FORM: ADJ (kareem, kiraam, akram) = the bearer characterized by the quality; V(II) karrama and V(IV) akrama = causative "cause/treat as possessing high worth" (the honoring act is morphological causation, not the root); N(IV) mukram/mukarram = passive "one made worth-bearing," and maṣdar ikraam = the abstract act of according worth. Subtract these and the constant "high esteem-worthy value" remains. CONSTRUCTION: the ʿalā in 17:62 (karramta ʿalayya) supplies the comparative/over-vector (elevation relative to another) — that comparison is from the preposition, not from krm, which supplies only the worth; the iḍāfa dhu'l-...-ikraam (55:27/78) supplies possession; direct-object frames on akrama supply the honoree. PARTICIPANTS: subjects/objects range over God, angels, humans, Iblis, plants, scriptures, letters, provisions, thrones, dwellings, scrolls — this wide spread proves the root itself fixes only "elevated worth," never a particular entity-type. CONTEXT: eschatological reward, patriarchal narrative, scripture self-description, polemic/theology supply domain; the residue is domain-invariant.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: The hardest case is 56:44:4:1 "laa baaridin wa laa kareem" — the shade/repast of the damned is "neither cool nor kareem." Here krm is (a) negated and (b) predicated of an unpleasant inanimate thing, which could look like a bare sense of "good/beneficial" rather than "worth/nobility." It reconciles cleanly: negation operates ON the invariant, not against it — the verse denies that the item possesses any esteem-worthy/beneficial value, so the residue "elevated worth" is exactly what is being withheld. The polarity is supplied by laa (construction); the residue is untouched. A secondary hard case, 89:15's akramani read against the following ahaanani (debased me), corroborates the residue: krm is the raising-in-worth whose lexical opposite is debasement, confirming direction (up in worth), not mere giving.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: The strongest alternative is that the core is GENEROSITY / open-handed giving (the salient classical sense of karam). Internal evidence arbitrates against it: the majority of occurrences predicate krm of things that give nothing — a throne (23:116), a plant-kind (26:7; 31:10), a letter (27:29), scripture (56:77), a station (26:58), a messenger's speech (69:40) — where "generous" is incoherent but "of high/noble worth" fits. Generosity is at best a special case of worth manifested in one participant-type (God, a host), not the invariant. A second alternative, that the core is the relational act HONORING, is closer but still secondary: adjectival uses (qurʾaan kareem, ʿarsh kareem) attribute intrinsic quality with no honorer in view, and the verbs themselves are causatives BUILT on that quality ("make-to-have-worth"). Thus intrinsic elevated worth is the more fundamental center from which both honoring (recognition of worth) and generosity (worth in action) derive.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Nearest semantic neighbors: (1) faDl (favor/preferment) — decisively separable, since 17:70 pairs both: "karramnaa banii aadama ... wa faDDalnaahum ʿalā katheer" — krm = ennobling with intrinsic worth, faDl = comparative surplus/preference OVER others; krm needs no comparison class, faDl does. (2) jalaal (awe-inspiring majesty) — paired yet distinct in 55:27/78 (dhu'l-jalaali wa'l-ikraam): jalaal is overwhelming grandeur that induces awe, ikraam is worth that induces esteem/honor. (3) sharaf/nobility of rank — overlaps but is rank-relational; krm is worth-intrinsic (a plant or scripture is kareem without social rank). (4) Hamd (praise) — the response to good acts, whereas krm is the standing worth prior to any praise. Falsifiability: the account fails if any occurrence required krm to mean bare quantity/abundance, mere transfer of goods with no worth/elevation dimension, or attributed krm to something the verse simultaneously marks as base/worthless in the same respect — none occurs.
internal_discovery.rationale: A single non-empty contribution — "elevated, esteem-worthy value/nobility" — is surface-recoverable in all 47 occurrences without forcing. It holds across the stative adjective (29 ADJ + variants), the elative (49:13; 96:3), the substantive plural kiraam (25:72; 80:16; 82:11), the causatives karrama (2) and akrama (4), and the derived passives/maṣdar mukram/mukarram/ikraam (N(IV) 7 + ADJ(IV) 1 + ADJ(II) 1). The form-families differ only in morphological direction (bearer of worth vs. conferrer/recipient of worth), which is subtracted as form, leaving the constant residue. The two apparent stress cases (negated 56:44; the debasement-contrast at 89:15) confirm rather than break the unity, since negation and antonymy operate on the very quality identified. The direction is determinate (worth up, opposite = debasement), and the root is sharply distinguished from faDl, jalaal, sharaf, and Hamd by internal pairings (notably 17:70 and 55:27/78). No occurrence remains unreconciled; inconsistent_refs is empty. Grounds for STRONG rather than MODERATE: the residue is directly readable at the surface everywhere, requires no metaphorical-bridge inference to unify, and is contrastively delimited against its neighbors by the text itself.

adversarial_verification.notes:
Refutation attempt: went through all 47. No true homonymy or semantic split exists — every token lives in the worth/nobility family, so REFUTED is not warranted. The adjectival core (kareem across angel 12:31, speech 17:23, rizq/ajr 22:50/8:4/33:31/34:4/36:11/57:11/57:18/8:74, throne 23:116, station 26:58/44:26, plant 26:7/31:10, letter 27:29, Qur'an 56:77, messengers 44:17/69:40/81:19, entrance 4:31, God 44:49/82:6/96:3), the elative (49:13/96:3), the plural substantive kiraam (25:72/80:16/82:11), the causatives karrama/akrama (17:62/17:70/89:15x2/89:17/12:21), and the mukram-/ikraam nominals (21:26/22:18/36:27/37:42/51:24/70:35/80:13/55:27/55:78) all reduce to elevated worth or the conferral of it.

Hardest cases + resolution: (1) 56:44 'laa baaridin wa-laa kareem' is the single genuinely awkward token — kareem is negated, modifies hell's smoke-shade in a wholly pejorative frame, and the natural gloss is 'wholesome/beneficial/pleasant,' NOT 'noble.' The candidate saves it only by stretching worth into 'has no good quality,' which leans on a benefit component it never names. (2) 27:40 'ghaniyyun kareem' — paired with ghaniyy (self-sufficient/rich), the dominant reading is Generous/Bountiful; this, plus 12:21 akrimii mathwaah (hospitality) and 55:27/78 al-ikraam, exposes a SYSTEMATIC underdetermination: the classical krm GENEROSITY/GIVING sense is a real distinct component the 'intrinsic worth' candidate collapses into 'worth.' These are strain points, not fatal splits, hence PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED.

Neighbor-root contrast: krm discriminates weakly-but-adequately — vs ʿzz (adds might/dominance; ʿazīz al-kareem in 44:49 stacks them precisely because they differ), vs faDl (surplus/preferment; 17:70 uses karramnaa AND faDDalnaa side by side, showing the speaker treats them as non-identical), vs majiid (glory). The candidate's elasticity — absorbing nobility, benefit, hospitality, and generosity all under one 'worth' label — is the chief risk; it is not a pure blob but is broader than the distinctively krm-specific 'noble-status + its conferral (honoring/hospitality/generous-giving).' Distinctiveness passes marginally; falsifiability holds (clear failure = a homonymous non-worth sense, and none occurs).
